name: barkeep
listed_description: Small C++ header to display async animations, counters, and progress bars.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable: README has no benchmarks or overhead figures (only 'Small' and 'minimally intrusive' wording, speed settings in the examples are display rates), the repo has no benchmark directory (barkeep/, docs/, python/, tests/), the issue search for performance/overhead/benchmark returns nothing, and a web search found no third-party overhead comparison against indicators, progressbar or tqdm. Lead claim word 'Small' is about size, not speed.

name: Blackhole
listed_description: Attribute-based logging framework, which is designed to be fast, modular and highly customizable.
reason: Directional claims only. README says the library was rewritten for performance and 'benchmark-driven development' and calls spdlog 'really fast, I checked', but gives no numbers. bench/ holds Google Benchmark micro-benchmarks of Blackhole's own components (logger, formatters, queue, record) with no competitor and no published results; CHANGELOG gives only self-relative gains (20-30 percent, 30 percent) against earlier Blackhole versions. The reckless logging benchmark page does not include Blackhole. Repo last commit 2018-12-12 (abandoned), MIT, 204 stars.

name: Bolt
listed_description: A C++ template library optimized for GPUs.
reason: Directional claim only ('high-performance library implementations', 'performance and power efficiency benefits'). README and wiki (Home, Current Work and Future Plans, OpenCL Device Vector Performance Parameters, Coding Style) have no numbers; bench/ and benchmarkPackage/ hold a benchmark harness but no published results or named baseline. The only numbers found are third-party and not in Bolt's favor: a search snippet of a 2016 sort/scan library comparison for GPUs (arXiv 1601.03144, blocked here) says Thrust, Bolt and Boost.Compute show no advantage for sorting and scanning and Boost.Compute beat HSA-Bolt on AMD FirePro S10000; a 2013 blog post on CPU vs GPU sorting (solarianprogrammer.com) is blocked. Last commit 2014-12-09 (abandoned), Apache-2.0, 379 stars. Lead category thread-pools-work-stealing does not fit (OpenCL/C++ AMP algorithm library).

name: buddy_alloc
listed_description: A single header buddy memory allocator for C with bounded allocation costs.
reason: No baseline numbers. README claims bounded (not fast) allocation cost and lists 'be a general purpose malloc() replacement' as a non-goal; its only tables are metadata-size tables. bench.c times only buddy_malloc filling a 1 GiB arena with time(NULL) in whole seconds and never runs malloc or any other allocator; issue #4 asking for a benchmark against malloc was closed with no comments or results, and issue #115 and the speed-improvement commits quote no figures. Last commit 2026-07-15 (active), 0BSD, 253 stars.
